claims: Coal is a combustible black sedimentary rock.
Coal is primarily used as a fossil fuel to generate electricity and produce steel.
Coal supplies about a quarter of the world's energy.
Coal is formed over millions of years from compressed, decayed plant matter in swamps.
Anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, and lignite.
Coal is extracted via surface or underground mining.
Coal originates from prehistoric vegetation (trees, ferns) in wetlands.
Prehistoric vegetation was buried under layers of dirt and rock 300 million years ago.
Over millions of years, heat and pressure (known as coalification) compressed organic matter, turning it first into peat, then into coal.
Coal acts as a store of energy originally captured from the sun.
Coal is ranked based on its carbon, moisture, and heat content.
Anthracite is the highest rank (hardest/most carbon), with a high, shiny, metallic luster.
Bituminous is a middle-rank, soft black coal used for generating electricity and making coke (for steel).
Subbituminous is black and dull, with low-to-moderate heating values, used for power generation.
Lignite is the lowest grade (brown coal), with high moisture and lower carbon content, primarily used for power.
Coal-fired power plants burn coal to heat water into high-pressure steam, which drives turbines to produce electricity.
Metallurgical (coking) coal is essential for reducing iron ore to iron in steel manufacturing.
Coal is used in cement production.
Coal is used in paper manufacturing.
Coal is sometimes used for heating.
Coal is found in seams within layered sedimentary rock formations worldwide.
Major coal deposits exist in the U.S., Russia, China, and India.
Surface mining (strip mining) is used when coal is near the surface, involving removing surface soil and rock (overburden).
Underground mining is used for deeper deposits, requiring shafts and tunnels for miners to extract the coal.
Coal mining destroys landscapes and disrupts ecosystems.
Burning coal releases carbon dioxide (CO2), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and heavy metals.
